items.title: Unused packages, large docker image
items.body: I was cleaning up te various Docker containers and I found that DAO has the largest image among all, even larger than Home Assistant itself: EMHASS, which is another package for prediction and cost optimisation, is over 1 GB smaller. NOW I understand why pulling the image was taking SO long. An automatic analysis of the potential changes to make it lighter follows below. I can code (slowly) and read code, but this kind of changes and package dependencies management is completely out of my skill set so I will just test the changes suggested by Claude and hope for the best. You can see the commit with all changes here: https://github.com/dewi-ny-je/day-ahead/commit/6cf06228423882a6e9526ecce0ffd4df226d36cd The image goes from 1.4 GB to 0.5 GB. My server has no GPU so nothing about running stuff there is maintained. In fact, even the users with a GPU wouldn't have used it in the image you ship, it's not enabled, just dead weight. I'm not sure how many people compile miplib, I'm not even sure as to why doing it. Anyway, `build_miplib.sh` now installs the build tools itself _the first time_ `use_self_compiled_miplib` compiles. So most users benefit from a smaller package, the few ones needing it can still get it. THIS IS UNTESTED. And I won't even test it, I don't care. Claude's text: --- The final image carries roughly **1.4 GB that it never uses**: about 0.9 GB inside the Python venv and about 0.5 GB of apt packages (compiler toolchain, npm/Node, `-dev` headers) in the runtime stage. ## Python venv (~1.4 GB today on amd64) | What | Size | Fix | Saving | |---|---|---|---| | `cbcbox/cbc_dist_debug_avx2` (amd64) / `cbc_dist_debug` (aarch64): a debug build of CBC, only used when `CBCBOX_BUILD=debug` is set, which the project never does | 334 MB amd64, 341 MB aarch64 | `rm -rf $VIRTUAL_ENV/lib/python3*/site-packages/cbcbox/cbc_dist_debug*` in the builder after install | **~335 MB** | | `nvidia-nccl-cu13`: CUDA multi-GPU library pulled in by `xgboost` on Linux; the code never uses a GPU | 345 MB (both arches) | replace `xgboost` with `xgboost-cpu` (same version, same `import xgboost`, no NCCL dependency) | **~345 MB** | | `xgboost` itself (GPU kernels) | 84 MB | same swap, `xgboost-cpu` wheel is 6 MB vs 58 MB | **~70 MB** | | Shared libraries inside cbcbox stored three times (`libX.so`, `.so.0`, `.so.0.0.0` are full copies, wheels can't hold symlinks) | 212 MB for `cbc_dist` + `cbc_dist_avx2`, only 80 MB unique | replace duplicates with symlinks in the builder (small shell loop, or `rdfind -makesymlinks`) | ~130 MB | | Unused MySQL drivers: `mysql-connector-python` (63 MB), `mysql` → `mysqlclient`, `mariadb`. Only `pymysql` is used (`lib/db_manager.py:111`) | ~65 MB | drop the three lines from `requirements.txt` | ~65 MB, and no more C compiles of mysqlclient/mariadb on every build | | `tests/` folders of pandas, scipy, numpy, matplotlib | ~40 MB | `find … -type d -name tests -prune -exec rm -rf {} +` | ~40 MB (optional) | Venv after these: roughly **0.45 GB** instead of 1.4 GB. ## Runtime apt packages (~770 MB today, ~230–260 MB needed) The runtime stage reinstalls almost everything the builder needed: - `npm` (pulls in nodejs plus ~370 node-* packages): **~195 MB**. Only the built JS in `app/static/build` is used at runtime. - `gcc g++ libmariadb-dev libjpeg-dev libffi-dev libnauty-dev coinor-libcgl-dev`: **~320 MB**. The wheels already bundle their own libs; headers and compilers are only needed by `prog/build_miplib.sh` (the optional `use_self_compiled_miplib`). - `python3-pip` and apt `gunicorn` (the venv has its own gunicorn, first on PATH): ~10 MB. - `apt-get upgrade -y` each build: small, but makes builds non-reproducible. Keeping `git`, `wget`, `nano` costs ~28 MB; fine to keep. **The one real trade-off** is `use_self_compiled_miplib`: `build_miplib.sh` needs gcc, g++, make, git, wget. Two options: 1. *(recommended)* install the toolchain on demand at the top of `build_miplib.sh` (`apt-get update && apt-get install -y --no-install-recommends gcc g++ make git wget`). It only runs once, since the result is saved to `/config/miplib`. Costs one extra download for the few users who enable it. 2. Keep gcc/g++ in the image and only drop npm and the `-dev` packages: saves ~200 MB instead of ~500 MB. ## Build time - Removing `mysql`/`mariadb`/`mysqlclient` removes the only source compiles in the pip step (they have no Linux wheels), so the builder also no longer needs `gcc g++ libmariadb-dev`. Probably 1–2 minutes per arch, more on aarch64. - The runtime stage currently installs ~540 apt packages every uncached build; the slim set is ~95. That's most of the runtime stage's time. - Optional: build the Vite bundle in its own small `node:XX-slim` stage. BuildKit then runs it in parallel with the Python stage, and the builder drops `npm` too. - Optional: add `--mount=type=cache,target=/root/.cache/uv` to the pip step and use `uv` from `ghcr.io/astral-sh/uv` instead of `pip install uv` / `pip uninstall uv`. Small gain; GHA layer cache already covers the unchanged-requirements case. ## Overall estimate | | Today | After | |---|---|---| | Venv | ~1.4 GB | ~0.45 GB | | Runtime apt (on top of base) | ~770 MB | ~250 MB | | **Image (uncompressed, approx.)** | **~2.3 GB** | **~0.8–0.9 GB** |

items.title: Server images keep unused packages and privileged programs, the amazonlinux2023 image gets no updates, and customers get no VEX
items.body:
The Debian runtime image (`build/runtime/Dockerfile`) purges login, passwd and util-linux but keeps the packages only they used: PAM (`libpam-runtime`, `libpam-modules`, `libpam-modules-bin`, `libpam0g`), `login.defs`, `sysvinit-utils`, and libraries that only purged packages needed (`libsqlite3-0`, `libsemanage2`, `libsepol2`, `libbsd0`).

The Amazon Linux 2023 server image is built from `amazonlinux:2023.12.20260817.0`. dnf on Amazon Linux only sees the repository release of its image, so the server stage's `dnf update -y` installs nothing, including the `openssl-libs` update.

The rhel9 and amazonlinux2023 server images ship setuid and setgid programs (su, mount, newgrp, unix_chkpwd…) and file capabilities (newuidmap, newgidmap) that nothing in them uses.

With TLS on, the rhel9 server image accepts finite-field Diffie-Hellman key exchange, in TLS 1.2 and TLS 1.3.

With `TLS=1`, `run.sh` creates and `chown`s files as root in a directory `falkordb` can write to, and follows links there.

No workflow scans the rhel9 and amazonlinux2023 server images: `security-scan` in `_ci-pipeline.yml` covers the Debian `falkordb` image only.

Scanners show customers CVEs in our images' OS packages that have no fixed version, and we publish no statement on whether they affect FalkorDB.

items.title: Release and CI hardening: tests before release, `latest` tag, permissions, pinned actions
items.body:
- `release.yml` builds images and binaries from the tag with no tests or lint, tags every run `latest` (including a re-run of an old tag via `workflow_dispatch`, which silently downgrades deployments that track `latest`), builds `linux/amd64` only, and hides upload failures with `|| echo`.
- `release.yml` and `create-release.yml` grant `contents: write` (and unused `packages: write`) to every job, pin actions to major tags rather than SHAs — including the ones holding Docker Hub secrets — and paste workflow inputs into `run:` scripts before validating them.
- The migration tool's CI runs only `go vet` (no golangci-lint, no coverage floor) and uses Go 1.23 while releases build with 1.27; `task tools`, CI and CLAUDE.md name three different golangci-lint versions.
- PR workflows have no `concurrency: cancel-in-progress`.

items.title: Lua 'unused import' detector reports string literals as imports; documented suppression form detector::*::rule can't match IDs with ::line suffix
items.body:
Two related quirks hit while running desloppify 1.0 (`pip install desloppify[full]`) on a pure-Lua project (a JVM interpreter: 42 module-part files, `return function(M, P) ... end` factories, natives registered by string keys — no `require()` anywhere by design).

## 1. Lua `unused` detector reports string literals as "unused imports"

`desloppify scan --path packages/xjvm` produced 244 + 239 (after rescan) `unused_import` findings, all of them string literals:

```
Unused import: ]                          bench/steps.lua:6
Unused import: t                          bench/steps.lua:16        # load(src, "=" .. p, "t")
Unused import: cannot load xjvm core ...  bench/steps.lua:25        # assert message
Unused import: <f                         src/01_util_format.lua:69 # string.pack format
Unused import: >d                         src/02_reader_desc.lua:52 # string.unpack format
Unused import: UTF-16BE                   src/26/27_*.lua           # charset-name table keys
```

Every flagged site is an argument string (assert messages, `load` modes, `string.pack/unpack` format specifiers, table keys). The detector appears to extract "import-like" tokens from string content. All 483 were false positives; I suppressed them, but the detector is effectively non-functional on Lua code with this shape, and the autofixer would corrupt code if applied.

## 2. Documented suppression form `detector::*::rule` cannot match IDs with a `::line` suffix

`desloppify suppress --help` recommends: *"Use detector::*::rule to keep a suppression across file moves."* But `matched_ignore_pattern` runs `fnmatch` against the **full issue ID**, and IDs carry a trailing line component:

- ID: `unused::packages/xjvm/bench/steps.lua::unused_import::6`
- Pattern `unused::*::unused_import` → no match (pattern ends where the ID has `::6`)

The suppression command succeeds, the config records the pattern, but nothing is ever filtered — findings reopen on the next scan. Working form: `unused::*::unused_import::*` (trailing `::*`). The inconsistency is easy to miss because `orphaned::*` works fine — orphaned IDs have no line suffix.

Environment: desloppify 1.0, Python 3.13.5, Linux. Happy to provide more repro detail if useful. Related: #939 (the `-lc` login-shell bug that masked the luacheck phase entirely on this machine).

items.title: chore: remove unused BilldDesk code, assets and dependencies

labels.name: priority: medium
labels.description: Standard roadmap priority; follow highest-priority feature work

items.body:
### What problem are you trying to solve?

About a fifth of `src/` (roughly 4,500 of 21,000 lines) is BilldDesk code that PalmDesk never reaches. It still has to be type-checked and reviewed and it adds attack surface, and some of it ships in the app.

**Unreachable modules**

- `src/api/`: `area`, `giftRecord`, `goods`, `live`, `liveConfig`, `livePlay`, `order`, `other`, `qiniuData`, `qqUser`, `signin`, `userLiveRoom`, `walletRecord`, `wechatUser`, `wsMessage`.
- Hooks and utilities: `hooks/webrtc/meetingTwo.ts`, `hooks/use-page.ts`, `hooks/use-upload.ts`, `utils/showBilldVersion.ts`, `utils/cookie/*`, and most of `utils/index.ts`.
- Views and components:
  - `views/privatizationDeployment` and `views/h5/privatizationDeployment`; their routes only redirect.
  - `views/remote/inviteInfo.vue`, `components/Notification` and `components/icons/*`.

**Code that can't run against the PalmDesk backend**

- `use-websocket.ts` sets up the live, PK, meeting, SRS and Tencent CSS hooks and handles upstream events. The backend accepts only ten desk events and disconnects any client that sends anything else ([`containers/backend/runtime/http.cjs#L62-L77`](https://github.com/Abreto/palmdesk/blob/cd366c1b6f3ce879219b38cbf3feffc59e6934f0/containers/backend/runtime/http.cjs#L62-L77)).
- The upstream update and disable modals call `/desk_version/*`, which the PalmDesk backend doesn't serve.

**Dependencies**

- `billd-deploy` and `vconsole` are never imported ([`package.json#L62`](https://github.com/Abreto/palmdesk/blob/cd366c1b6f3ce879219b38cbf3feffc59e6934f0/package.json#L62), [`#L73`](https://github.com/Abreto/palmdesk/blob/cd366c1b6f3ce879219b38cbf3feffc59e6934f0/package.json#L73)). `billd-deploy` pulls in cloud-storage SDKs and `node-ssh`.
- `js-cookie` and `spark-md5` are used only by dead code.
- `billd-html-webpack-plugin` is a *runtime* dependency ([`#L63`](https://github.com/Abreto/palmdesk/blob/cd366c1b6f3ce879219b38cbf3feffc59e6934f0/package.json#L63)) that pulls in webpack 5 and Vite 4 only to inject a build banner.
- `billd-utils` is used only for a few small helpers that are easy to inline.
- Unused development tools:
  - `ts-node`, `trash`, `rimraf`
  - `vite-plugin-commonjs`, `vite-plugin-electron-renderer`, `@vitejs/plugin-legacy`
  - `@electron/rebuild` and the `@vue/eslint-config-*` packages
  - The `cz` script points to `cz-conventional-changelog`, which isn't declared.

**Shipped inside the app**

electron-builder packs production `dependencies` into `app.asar`. Every installer therefore probably includes the unused packages above, along with renderer libraries that Vite has already bundled.

**A build banner in every page**

`BilldHtmlWebpackPlugin` ([`vite.config.ts#L137`](https://github.com/Abreto/palmdesk/blob/cd366c1b6f3ce879219b38cbf3feffc59e6934f0/vite.config.ts#L137), [`#L141`](https://github.com/Abreto/palmdesk/blob/cd366c1b6f3ce879219b38cbf3feffc59e6934f0/vite.config.ts#L141)) runs `git` during the build. It then adds an inline `<script>` to `index.html` that logs:

- the commit subject and branch;
- the committer's name and email;
- the Node version.

The inline script also stands in the way of a strict `script-src` CSP.

**Other leftovers**

- The `/betaapi` and `/prodapi` dev proxies ([`vite.config.ts#L173-L194`](https://github.com/Abreto/palmdesk/blob/cd366c1b6f3ce879219b38cbf3feffc59e6934f0/vite.config.ts#L173-L194)).
- A Linux AppImage target ([`electron-builder.cjs#L49-L54`](https://github.com/Abreto/palmdesk/blob/cd366c1b6f3ce879219b38cbf3feffc59e6934f0/electron-builder.cjs#L49-L54)), although Linux hosts aren't supported.
- Main-process IPC handlers that nothing in `src/` calls: `powerSaveBlockerStart`, `windowMaximize`, `setWindowBounds`, `getWindowTitlebarHeight`, `getWindowPosition`, `handleMoveScreenRightBottom` and `showTargetApplication`. About half of the `IPC_EVENT` keys are unused.
- Unreferenced images: `my-wechat.png`, `arrow_down.png`, `copy.png`, `edit.png`, `refresh.png`, `sync.png`, `view.png` and `view_off.png`.
- `test/test.{js,ts,json,html}`.
- Upstream admin messages in `src/locales`.

### Proposed behavior and alternatives

- Delete the unreachable files and branches, and reduce `use-websocket.ts` to the ten events the backend accepts.
- Remove the unused packages.
  - Replace `billd-html-webpack-plugin` with `pkg.version`, which `vite.config.ts` already defines.
  - Replace `billd-utils` with small local helpers.
- Keep only main-process runtime modules such as `@nut-tree-fork/nut-js` in `dependencies`, and move renderer-only libraries to `devDependencies`. Check the result with `npx @electron/asar list`.
- Remove the Linux target, or make it fail with a clear message.
- Add [`knip`](https://knip.dev) to CI so unused files and exports don't creep back.
- Keep upstream docs (`doc/`, `readme_img/`, `README_OpenSource.md`) only where attribution needs them. MIT requires only the licence text, so `THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md` can link to the upstream project instead.

**Acceptance criteria**

- `knip` reports no unused files or dependencies, apart from an explicit ignore list.
- `app.asar` contains no `billd-deploy`, `vconsole`, `webpack` or `vite`.
- The built `index.html` contains no inline script.

items.title: CPU-only torch for Linux: 16 unused CUDA packages cost 8.4 GB in CI and on the worker
items.body:
## Problem

GeecsBluesky's `optimize` extra pulls torch transitively (`xopt` → `botorch` → `torch`), and PyPI's default **Linux** wheel is the CUDA build. That drags in 15 `nvidia-*` packages plus `triton`:

```
nvidia-cublas-cu12       nvidia-cudnn-cu12      nvidia-cusolver-cu12
nvidia-cuda-cupti-cu12   nvidia-cufft-cu12      nvidia-cusparse-cu12
nvidia-cuda-nvrtc-cu12   nvidia-cufile-cu12     nvidia-cusparselt-cu12
nvidia-cuda-runtime-cu12 nvidia-curand-cu12     nvidia-nccl-cu12
nvidia-nvjitlink-cu12    nvidia-nvshmem-cu12    nvidia-nvtx-cu12   triton
```

**Nothing ever loads them.** No GitHub runner has a GPU, and (as of 2026-09-18) neither does the worker box.

### Measured cost

- **CI:** GeecsBluesky's download set is **8.4 GB** against GitHub's 10 GB per-repo cache cap. In #940 this was large enough that caching it evicted *every other leg's cache* — the next run reported `Cache not found for input keys` on all eleven legs. That leg is now excluded from caching entirely (`.github/workflows/unit-tests.yml`), and pays ~105 s of install on every run. It is the critical path of the whole workflow.
- **Deployment:** the same dead weight installs on the worker on every deploy — install time, disk, and packages that never execute. This is arguably the bigger prize and is independent of CI.

For scale: the same package set on macOS, where torch has no CUDA build, is a **1.6 GB** venv.

## What was tried in #940 (and reverted)

Three forms, none of which works. Recorded so they are not re-walked.

**1. Single source for all platforms.**
```toml
[[tool.poetry.source]]
name = "pytorch-cpu"
url = "https://download.pytorch.org/whl/cpu"
priority = "explicit"

torch = { version = ">=2.4,<2.11", source = "pytorch-cpu", optional = true }
```
Lock came out clean (0 CUDA entries), but **breaks macOS**: `poetry install --extras optimize` exits 1 with *"38 wheel(s) were skipped as your project's environment does not support the identified abi tags"*. Cause: the index publishes Linux wheels as `X.Y.Z+cpu` and macOS wheels as plain `X.Y.Z`; a lock entry holds **one** version, and `2.10.0+cpu` has no macOS wheel.

**2. Platform split** (Linux → CPU index, macOS → PyPI), with `platform_system` on both arms.
macOS installs fine, but **CUDA still installs on Linux** — confirmed on a runner, 15 nvidia packages + triton. Cause: Poetry writes the *union* of markers into the lock and installs a package when its own lock marker evaluates true. The macOS arm's torch declares the nvidia deps with `platform_system == "Linux"` markers, which are true on Linux even though that arm is never selected there. (Tried with `sys_platform` too — worse, since Poetry cannot relate `sys_platform` and `platform_system` at all.)

**3. Both arms on the CPU index**, macOS pinned `==2.10.0`.
The macOS arm resolved back to PyPI anyway (PEP 440: `==2.10.0` matches `2.10.0+cpu`), and the lock still carried all 19 entries.

**Root cause:** Poetry cannot express *"this transitive dependency, from this index, on this platform only."*

## Options

1. **CI-only overlay** — `poetry export` + `pip install --index-url https://download.pytorch.org/whl/cpu torch`, bypassing the lock for torch alone. Fixes CI, not deployment.
2. **`uv`** — handles per-platform index pinning properly via `[tool.uv.sources]`. A real option given it is close to a drop-in for Poetry's resolve, but it is a toolchain change for the whole monorepo.
3. **Wait** for Poetry to support local-version-aware sources.
4. **Do nothing** — accept ~105 s per CI run and the deploy footprint.

## If this is picked up

Add a guard so the pin cannot regress silently on a future relock. #940 had a working one (reverted with the rest); the shape is:

```yaml
if poetry run pip list --format=freeze 2>/dev/null | grep -iE '^(nvidia-|triton)=='; then
  echo "::error::CUDA packages installed — the CPU-only torch pin regressed"
  exit 1
fi
```

This is what caught form 2 — the symptom is otherwise just "install is slow", which nobody notices.

**Coverage note:** dropping the `optimize` extra from CI is *not* an alternative. Those tests sit behind `importorskip`, so without the extra they silently skip and the check goes green saying nothing — #866 exactly. They exercise ask/tell and the measurement compiler, not GPU maths (32 tests, ~19 s), and pass identically on CPU-only torch.

**Priority:** P2

**Type:** Maintenance / performance improvement

**Problem and impact**

All five platform/architecture server executables are unconditional Flutter assets, while runtime loads only the current platform's single binary. Release packaging archives/copies the Flutter bundle without removing the other binaries. Thus a Linux amd64 install carries Windows, both macOS architectures, and Linux arm64 executables it can never use. This materially increases installed size and release artifact construction/transfer volume.

**When it happens**

Any desktop release or installation built from the current asset manifest.

**Evidence**

The original whole-project review recorded the following evidence and validation limits:

Exact sizes from the checkout sum to **276,777,886 bytes** (about 264 MiB). Linux amd64 requires 55,845,156 bytes, leaving **220,932,730 bytes** (about 211 MiB) of unused raw assets. Compressed download overhead depends on archive compression and was not measured.

Asset sizes measured; unconditional inclusion and packaging path source-confirmed. A new release bundle was not built.

**Suggested fix**

Prepare a build-specific asset manifest/staging step that includes only the target OS/architecture server binary and keeps runtime asset lookup consistent. Do not remove platform binaries from source without replacing cross-platform build support.

The `hermes-compiler` npm package, a dependency of `react-native` (0.88.0 and current nightlies depend on `hermes-compiler@260318099.0.4`), ships `hermesc` for Windows, macOS and Linux in one package, with no `os`/`cpu` fields and no per-platform optional packages. Publish `hermes-compiler-<os>-<cpu>` packages declared as `optionalDependencies` with `os`/`cpu` fields (the esbuild / napi-rs / swc pattern), so package managers install only the host binary. `hermes-compiler` itself would only resolve the right binary path.

items.title: Boot time: profile every stage from power-on to forwarding, cut the long waits, track per change
items.body:
Mirror of awto-tl-st1008f#114 (and #26: "OpenWrt RAM-boot is slow").

## Baseline (2026-10-14, kernel0 flash boot, console capture `tmp/logs/console/us48-20261014-083748.log`)

- `bootm` → userspace shell: 59 s. C.
- U-Boot `bootdelay` 3 s; `sf read` of the uImage from QSPI; uImage CRC check.
- RAM boot via `loady` ymodem: 8–10 min at 115200 (460800 baud switch in `console.py`).
- No forwarding stage yet (no fabric driver) → "power-on to forwarding" ends at shell for now; extend when #4 lands.

## Stages to timestamp

| Stage | Marker | Suspected cost |
|---|---|---|
| Power-on → U-Boot banner | console first byte | DDR init + shmoo |
| Banner → `bootm` | `Hit any key` + 3 s | bootdelay, `sf read` at 12.5 MHz (DTS) |
| `bootm` → `Starting kernel` | U-Boot CRC + LZMA? | data CRC over ~6 MB, uncompress |
| Kernel decompress → `Booting Linux` | earlycon | zImage self-decompress, caches |
| Kernel init → `/init` | `initcall_debug` | PCIe link wait, I2C probe, SPI-NOR probe, random |
| `/init` → procd → shell | procd log | initramfs unpack (size!), preinit failsafe wait, services |
| → ports forwarding | first frame forwarded | future: SDK-free switch init, PHY AN, STP forward delay |

## Method (from 1008#114)

- `scripts/boot_profile.py`: timestamp each console line on the host (monotonic, from the tio socket), match stage markers, write `tmp/logs/boot-profile-<YYYYMMDD-HHMMSS>.tsv`; table per run in this issue.
- Kernel: `initcall_debug printk.time=1` in a profiling build; `bootgraph`-style sort of the slowest initcalls.
- Userspace: procd `-d`, `logread` timestamps.
- Track per commit: every change that moves a stage > 1 s gets a row here.

## Candidate cuts (check, don't assume)

- QSPI read speed: DTS 12.5 MHz vs MX25L25635E rated max (dual/quad read in U-Boot `sf` + Linux spi-mem) — rated-max rule.
- Kernel/initramfs compression (LZMA vs LZ4/XZ trade on 400 MHz A9), initramfs size (drop unused packages).
- Preinit failsafe wait, `bootdelay` (U-Boot env is off-limits: no `saveenv` → leave it).
- PCIe link training wait in `pcie-iproc`.
- CPU clock: A9 at 400 MHz — is that HR2 rated max for this SKU? (A9 PLL `brcm,hr2-armpll`) → hardware-inventory issue.

## Known cuts from 1008#114 (re-measure here, don't copy numbers)

- procd runs init scripts one at a time → sum of script times = boot time. Stamp every init script via patched `/etc/rc.common` + a `/lib/preinit/01_us48_stamp` hook (port `build_openwrt.py rc_common_stamps`).
- Preinit failsafe network + key window: `pi_ifname=none`, 1 s window (1008: 10.3 s → 5.0 s).
- dropbear RAM-boot key generation (1008: 7–21 s on MIPS) → START after network, ship the init script itself (postinst recreates rc.d links).
- One change per measured boot; separate baselines per boot path (kernel0 flash vs `loady` RAM).
- US-48 has no network under OpenWrt yet → 1008's SSH-pull `boot_timeline.py` needs a console variant (dmesg + logread over the tio socket at the end of boot).

## Next steps

- [ ] Write `boot_profile.py` (or port `boot_timeline.py` with a US-48 `STAGES` regex list + `compare A B`), record the baseline table (3 runs, cold + warm).
- [ ] Rank stages; one sub-issue per cut > 2 s.

**Problem and impact**

No Dart source or test imports `flutter_discord_rpc` or `smooth_video_progress`. Video playback uses `package:fvp/mdk.dart` directly (`lib/core/services/video/video_service.dart:8`), and its progress UI is maintained by the app's own timer and slider (`lib/presentation/widgets/styled/unyo_video_controls.dart:51–55`, `:278–289`). This is concrete native/dependency work for an integration that the application does not execute. The unused progress package also retains a `flutter_hooks` dependency with no app consumer.

**When it happens**

Dependency resolution and desktop packaging/builds, even when the user never enables Discord presence.

**Evidence**

The original whole-project review recorded the following evidence and validation limits:

Whole-project package-import inventory found zero imports of either package. Searching their names outside generated files finds only `pubspec.yaml`; the desktop generated CMake lists confirm that Dart tree shaking does not eliminate the Discord build integration. If the sibling legitimately declares either package, normal transitive resolution should retain that dependency for its owner.

Remove these two unused direct dependencies and regenerate dependency/plugin metadata through Flutter tooling. items.title: [Bug]: lazyBarrel reports MISSING_EXPORT for an unused named re-export from an `export *` barrel
items.body:
### Reproduction link or steps

https://github.com/BlankParticle/rolldown-lazy-barrel-repro

```sh
pnpm install
pnpm repro
```

```js
// entry.js
import { value } from "lib/mod.js";
console.log(value);

// packages/lib/mod.js        (package "lib", "sideEffects": false)
export const value = 1;
export { Foo as LibFoo } from "barrel"; // unused by the entry

// packages/barrel/index.js   (package "barrel", "sideEffects": false)
export * from "./foo.js";

// packages/barrel/foo.js
export class Foo {}
```

`build.mjs` bundles `entry.js` with `experimental: { lazyBarrel: false }` and then `{ lazyBarrel: true }`.

### What is expected?

Both builds succeed. `barrel` exports `Foo` through `export * from "./foo.js"`, so `export { Foo as LibFoo } from "barrel"` is valid, and it bundles fine with `lazyBarrel: false`.

### What is actually happening?

With `lazyBarrel: true` the build fails:

```
[MISSING_EXPORT] "Foo" is not exported by "packages/barrel/index.js".
   ╭─[ packages/lib/mod.js:4:10 ]
   │
 4 │ export { Foo as LibFoo } from "barrel";
   │          ─┬─
   │           ╰─── Missing export
───╯
```

It needs all three of:
- the importing module (`lib/mod.js`) is in a `"sideEffects": false` package and is imported for one of its own local exports
- it has a named re-export whose target barrel only provides the name through `export *`
- nothing in the bundle uses the re-exported name

Any one of these makes the build pass:
- `"sideEffects": true` on `lib`
- `import { Foo } from "barrel"` instead of re-exporting it
- re-exporting from the defining module (`export { Foo } from "barrel/foo.js"`)
- the entry using `LibFoo`
- `lib/mod.js` being a pure barrel imported through its package entry

items.title: Split [ci].deploy so wheel and Conan publishing can be enabled independently
items.body:
## Summary

`[ci].deploy` is a single switch over **both** publishing paths. On a tag push it emits, together:

- `Wheel Deploy` — pushes the wheel to devpi
- `Conan Deploy - Linux` / `Conan Deploy - Windows` — push the Conan packages to the Conan remote

There is no way to keep one and drop the other.

## Why it matters

A library whose only consumer is Python has no use for its Conan packages. Nothing links them; they are published on every tag, take up space on a shared remote, and add two jobs to every release pipeline for no benefit.

**xmssnap** is the concrete case. Python is its sole consumer — the `.pyd` is the only way to use the library, and no C++ code links it, not even dynamically. Its Conan packages exist purely as a build artifact of producing the wheel.

The reverse pairing is plausible too: a C++-only library with `pybind = False` still gets a `Wheel Deploy` job emitted whenever `[ci].deploy` is on.

## Suggestion

Split the flag, keeping `[ci].deploy` as the master switch so nothing changes by default:

```toml
[ci]
deploy = true          # unchanged: master switch for the Deploy stage
conan_deploy = false   # new, default true
wheel_deploy = true    # new, default true
```

Both new keys default to `true`, so every existing project renders exactly what it does today. `deploy = false` continues to drop the whole stage regardless.

A guard is probably worth it for `deploy = true` with both sub-flags `false`, which would emit an empty Deploy stage — the same shape as the two guards added in #90 for `[ci].linux`.

## Priority

Low. This is a nice-to-have, not a blocker — publishing unused Conan packages is wasteful but harmless, and xmssnap will ship with `deploy = true` and simply carry them. Filing it so the decision is recorded rather than rediscovered.

## Context

Found while converting xmssnap to Conan 2, alongside the three gaps addressed in #90. Reviewed with @gagelarsen, who asked that this one be tracked as a future feature rather than fixed now.

items.title: Minimizing AWS Volatile Memory on the EC2
items.body:
# Issue: High Volatile Memory Usage on AWS Instance

## Summary
AWS EC2 instance experiencing high RAM consumption requiring optimization strategies to reduce memory footprint and improve performance.


## Environment
- Platform: AWS EC2
- Issue Type: Resource Optimization

---

## Problem Description

The AWS instance is experiencing excessive volatile memory (RAM) usage that needs to be minimized to:
- Reduce costs by avoiding instance size upgrades
- Improve application performance
- Prevent out-of-memory errors
- Optimize resource utilization

---

## Investigation Steps

### 1. Memory Monitoring

First, identify current memory consumers:

```bash
# Check current memory usage
free -h

# See top memory consumers
top -o %MEM

# Detailed process memory info
ps aux --sort=-%mem | head -20

# Check memory usage over time
vmstat 1 10
```

### 2. Identify Specific Issues

- [ ] Check for memory leaks in applications
- [ ] Identify unused services running
- [ ] Review application memory configurations
- [ ] Check for excessive caching
- [ ] Review log file sizes and rotation

---

## Proposed Solutions

### Immediate Actions (Quick Wins)

#### Clear System Caches
```bash
# Drop caches (safe operation)
sync
sudo echo 3 > /proc/sys/vm/drop_caches
```

#### Remove Unused Packages
```bash
# For Ubuntu/Debian
sudo apt autoremove
sudo apt clean

# For Amazon Linux/RHEL
sudo yum autoremove
sudo yum clean all
```

#### Stop Unnecessary Services
```bash
# List all running services
systemctl list-units --type=service --state=running

# Disable unused services
sudo systemctl stop <service-name>
sudo systemctl disable <service-name>
```

---

### Short-term Solutions

#### 1. Configure Swap Space

Add swap to handle memory spikes without upgrading instance:

```bash
# Create 2GB swap file
sudo dd if=/dev/zero of=/swapfile bs=1G count=2
sudo chmod 600 /swapfile
sudo mkswap /swapfile
sudo swapon /swapfile

# Make permanent by adding to /etc/fstab
echo '/swapfile none swap sw 0 0' | sudo tee -a /etc/fstab
```

**Swap Configuration Guidelines:**
- General purpose: Swap = 1x RAM (for instances with <2GB RAM)
- Memory-intensive: Swap = 0.5x RAM
- High-performance: Minimal or no swap

#### 2. Linux Kernel Tuning

Edit `/etc/sysctl.conf`:

```bash
# Reduce swappiness (0-100, lower = less swap usage)
vm.swappiness=10

# Reduce cache pressure
vm.vfs_cache_pressure=50

# Limit dirty page cache
vm.dirty_ratio=10
vm.dirty_background_ratio=5

# Apply changes
sudo sysctl -p
```

#### 3. Service Optimization

**Web Servers:**
```bash
# Switch from Apache to Nginx (more memory efficient)
# Or optimize Apache:
# - Reduce MaxRequestWorkers
# - Use mpm_event instead of mpm_prefork
```

**Databases:**
- PostgreSQL: Reduce `shared_buffers` (default 25% of RAM)
- MySQL: Optimize `innodb_buffer_pool_size`
- Redis: Set `maxmemory` limit with eviction policy

---

### Long-term Solutions

#### 1. Application-Level Optimization

**Java Applications:**
```bash
# Optimize JVM heap sizes
-Xmx512m -Xms256m  # Adjust based on needs
-XX:MaxMetaspaceSize=256m
-XX:+UseG1GC  # More efficient garbage collector
```

**Node.js Applications:**
```bash
# Limit V8 heap size
node --max-old-space-size=512 app.js
```

**Python Applications:**
- Use memory profilers: `memory_profiler`, `tracemalloc`
- Implement connection pooling
- Use generators instead of lists for large datasets

#### 2. Caching Strategy

```bash
# Install Redis for application-level caching
sudo yum install redis -y
sudo systemctl start redis

# Configure Redis memory limit
maxmemory 256mb
maxmemory-policy allkeys-lru
```

#### 3. Monitoring and Alerting

**CloudWatch Metrics:**
- Set alarms for MemoryUtilization > 80%
- Monitor swap usage
- Track per-process memory consumption

**Install Monitoring Tools:**
```bash
# Install CloudWatch agent
wget https://s3.amazonaws.com/amazoncloudwatch-agent/linux/amd64/latest/amazon-cloudwatch-agent.deb
sudo dpkg -i amazon-cloudwatch-agent.deb
```

---

### AWS-Specific Optimizations

#### 1. Instance Right-Sizing

Consider these options:
- **Current approach**: Optimize software
- **If optimization insufficient**: 
  - Use memory-optimized instances (r6i, r6g family)
  - Enable AWS Compute Optimizer recommendations

#### 2. Auto Scaling

Configure Auto Scaling based on memory metrics:
```bash
# Create scaling policy based on memory
aws autoscaling put-scaling-policy \
  --auto-scaling-group-name my-asg \
  --policy-name memory-scale-up \
  --policy-type TargetTrackingScaling \
  --target-tracking-configuration file://memory-tracking.json
```

#### 3. Alternative Architectures

- **AWS Lambda**: For bursty, event-driven workloads
- **AWS Fargate**: Container workloads with automatic scaling
- **AWS RDS**: Managed database instead of self-hosted
- **ElastiCache**: Managed Redis/Memcached

---

## Implementation Checklist

### Phase 1: Assessment (Week 1)
- [ ] Document current memory usage baseline
- [ ] Identify top 10 memory consumers
- [ ] Review application logs for memory errors
- [ ] Analyze peak usage patterns

### Phase 2: Quick Optimizations (Week 1-2)
- [ ] Clear system caches
- [ ] Remove unused packages
- [ ] Stop unnecessary services
- [ ] Configure swap space
- [ ] Implement kernel tuning

### Phase 3: Application Optimization (Week 2-4)
- [ ] Optimize JVM/runtime settings
- [ ] Implement connection pooling
- [ ] Configure application-level caching
- [ ] Review and optimize database settings
- [ ] Implement memory limits per service

### Phase 4: Monitoring (Ongoing)
- [ ] Set up CloudWatch alarms
- [ ] Create memory usage dashboard
- [ ] Document memory optimization procedures
- [ ] Schedule monthly memory audits

---

## Success Metrics

- [ ] Reduce memory usage by 20-30%
- [ ] Eliminate out-of-memory errors
- [ ] Maintain memory utilization below 75%
- [ ] Improve application response times

---

## Resources

- [[AWS EC2 Memory Performance](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AWSEC2/latest/UserGuide/memory-optimized-instances.html)](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AWSEC2/latest/UserGuide/memory-optimized-instances.html)
- [[Linux Memory Management](https://www.kernel.org/doc/html/latest/admin-guide/mm/index.html)](https://www.kernel.org/doc/html/latest/admin-guide/mm/index.html)
- [[AWS CloudWatch Agent](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonCloudWatch/latest/monitoring/Install-CloudWatch-Agent.html)](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonCloudWatch/latest/monitoring/Install-CloudWatch-Agent.html)

---

## Notes

- Test all changes in a non-production environment first
- Monitor application performance after each optimization
- Document baseline metrics before making changes
- Keep rollback procedures ready

items.title: Binary installs drop the execute bit (processx bin/supervisor is not executable)
items.body:
## Summary

Binary installs drop the execute bit, so packages that ship executables can't run them. For **processx**, `bin/px`, `bin/sock` and `bin/supervisor` are installed `-rw-r--r--`. Anything that starts a process through processx then fails, including callr, chromote/webshot2 and pak.

## Reproduce

uvr 0.4.7 (release binary) on Ubuntu 24.04 (noble), R 4.5.3, non-root user, binaries from P3M:

```sh
mkdir p && cd p && uvr init && uvr add processx
ls -l .uvr/library/processx/bin/
# -rw-r--r-- px
# -rw-r--r-- sock
# -rw-r--r-- supervisor
```

The P3M tarball has them executable:

```sh
curl -fsSL -A "R/4.5.3 R (4.5.3 x86_64-pc-linux-gnu x86_64 linux-gnu)" \
  https://packagemanager.posit.co/cran/__linux__/noble/latest/src/contrib/processx_3.9.0.tar.gz | tar tvzf - | grep /bin/
# -rwxrwxr-x builder/builder 18568 2026-08-13 07:43 processx/bin/px
# -rwxrwxr-x builder/builder 14472 2026-08-13 07:43 processx/bin/sock
# -rwxrwxr-x builder/builder 14472 2026-08-13 07:43 processx/bin/supervisor
```

Downstream failure (chromote):

```
cannot start processx process '/tmp/p/.uvr/library/processx/bin/supervisor'
(system error 13, Permission denied) @unix/processx.c:651 (processx_exec)
```

`chmod +x .uvr/library/processx/bin/*` makes chromote and webshot2 work, so the mode is the only problem.

## Cause

`crates/uvr-core/src/installer/binary_install.rs` extracts entries manually and doesn't preserve permissions. The comments say so:

```rust
// NOTE: archive metadata-preservation settings are unused because
// extract_entry does manual file creation. R packages have no
// meaningful mtime/permissions to preserve.
```

```rust
// - mtime/permission preservation, which fails opaquely on some CI
//   filesystems and isn't meaningful for R packages anyway
```

Mode bits do matter for R packages that ship executables. processx is the most common (`bin/`), and others put tools under `exec/` or `bin/`. Same code on `main` at 3824ae3 (v0.4.8).

## Suggested fix

Keep the manual extraction, but after writing each file apply the entry's execute bits (for example `header.mode() & 0o111`, masked by the umask) with `std::fs::set_permissions`. If the call fails on an unusual filesystem, warn rather than fail. A regression test could install processx and check that `bin/supervisor` is executable.

## Related, minor

On noble, the sysreqs check warns that `textshaping`, `systemfonts` and `ragg` need `libfreetype6-dev`, even when `libfreetype-dev` is installed. Ubuntu 24.04 has no `libfreetype6-dev` package; the name is only a `Provides:` of `libfreetype-dev`, so a check by exact package name never passes. The binaries install and load fine. I can open this separately if you prefer.

items.title: workspace import not credited when exports point into dist/src and the build output exists
items.body:
### What happened?

A workspace package whose `exports` point into `dist/src/` (tsconfig `rootDir: "./"`, `outDir: "./dist"`) stops getting credit for imports from other workspaces once `dist/` is built. In the repro, `used` is imported by `app` but reported as unused.

It works without `dist/` on disk, and it also works with the flat layout (`rootDir: "./src"`, exports `./dist/index.js`). So the dist-to-src mapping seems to miss the extra `src/` segment when the built file exists. #3208 fixed the case where the output is missing.

We hit this in a pnpm monorepo where three packages use this layout and CI builds before fallow runs. The only workaround we found is `publicPackages`, which also hides real dead code inside those packages.

### Reproduction

```sh
mkdir repro && cd repro
echo '{ "name": "repro", "private": true }' > package.json
printf 'packages:\n  - packages/*\n' > pnpm-workspace.yaml
mkdir -p packages/lib/src packages/lib/dist/src packages/app/src packages/app/node_modules/@r
echo '{ "name": "@r/lib", "type": "module", "exports": { ".": { "types": "./dist/src/index.d.ts", "import": "./dist/src/index.js" } } }' > packages/lib/package.json
echo '{ "compilerOptions": { "rootDir": "./", "outDir": "./dist", "declaration": true }, "include": ["src"] }' > packages/lib/tsconfig.json
echo 'export const used = 1; export const unused = 2;' > packages/lib/src/index.ts
# what tsc emits for rootDir "./"
echo 'export const used = 1; export const unused = 2;' > packages/lib/dist/src/index.js
echo 'export declare const used: number; export declare const unused: number;' > packages/lib/dist/src/index.d.ts
echo '{ "name": "@r/app", "type": "module", "main": "src/main.ts", "dependencies": { "@r/lib": "workspace:*" } }' > packages/app/package.json
echo 'import { used } from "@r/lib"; console.log(used);' > packages/app/src/main.ts
ln -s ../../../lib packages/app/node_modules/@r/lib
fallow dead-code --include-entry-exports
```

```
● Unused exports (2)
  packages/lib/src/index.ts (2)
    :1 unused
    :1 used
```

`--include-entry-exports` is only there so the lib's entry exports get reported at all; we run with `includeEntryExports: true`.

### Expected behavior

Only `unused` is reported.

### Fallow version

3.35.0

### Operating system

Linux

# 前言

本文将介绍 Advanced Packaging Tool (APT) 包管理器，以及其在 Debian 系统及其衍生发行版（如 Ubuntu）中的配置方式和使用方法。我们将探讨如何配置 APT，包括软件源的设置和更新策略。我们还将深入了解 APT 的使用方式，包括通过命令行工具 apt 进行软件包的安装、升级和移除等操作。通过本文，读者将能够全面了解 APT 的功能和特性，并能够有效地使用 APT 管理软件包，提升系统的稳定性和安全性。

<!-- more -->

背景：

-   系统：Debian 12；

[⬆ back to top](#)

# APT

APT 是一个命令行工具，也是 Debian 系统和基于 Debian 的发行版（如 Ubuntu）中常用的软件包管理工具之一。它是 Advanced Packaging Tool（高级软件包工具）的缩写，旨在简化软件包的安装、升级和移除等操作。

[⬆ back to top](#)

# 常见的包管理器

| 包管理器 | 描述 |
| --- | --- |
| [**Advanced Packaging Tool (APT)**](https://wiki.debian.org/Apt) | APT 是 Debian 系统及其衍生发行版（如 Ubuntu）中的包管理器。它通过命令行工具 `apt` 提供软件包的安装、升级和移除等功能。 |
| [**dnf/yum**](https://dnf.readthedocs.io/en/latest/) | dnf（Dandified Yum）是 Fedora 系统及其衍生发行版中的包管理器，取代了旧的 Yum 包管理器。在较旧的 Fedora 和 CentOS 系统中，仍然可以使用 Yum 来进行包管理。 |
| [**Pacman**](https://wiki.archlinux.org/index.php/Pacman) | Pacman 是 Arch Linux 及其衍生发行版（如 Manjaro）中的包管理器。它使用简单的命令行工具来管理软件包，具有轻量且高效的特点。 |
| [**Homebrew**](https://brew.sh/) | Homebrew 是 macOS 系统上的包管理器，用于安装、更新和管理各种开源软件包。它具有简单易用的命令行界面，并提供了大量的软件包供用户选择。 |
| [**Chocolatey**](https://chocolatey.org/) | Chocolatey 是 Windows 系统上的包管理器，类似于 Linux 系统中的包管理器。它允许用户通过命令行界面来安装、升级和管理软件包。 |
| [**Snap**](https://snapcraft.io/) | Snap 是一种通用的软件打包和分发格式，可在多个 Linux 发行版上使用。Snap 提供了一个命令行工具来管理软件包，使得安装和更新软件变得更加简单和可靠。 |

[⬆ back to top](#)

# 常见命令

第三种命令是`apt`，它是APT的一种更简洁的命令行工具，自动处理软件包之间的依赖关系。它在一些较新的Debian和Ubuntu发行版中取代了`apt-get`命令，提供了更直观和用户友好的界面。

[⬆ back to top](#)

## 安装软件包

```shell
sudo apt install <package>
```

该命令用于安装指定的软件包。它会自动解析并安装所需的依赖关系。

[⬆ back to top](#)

## 升级已安装的软件包

```shell
sudo apt upgrade
```

该命令用于升级系统中已安装的软件包。它会检查可用的软件包更新并升级到最新版本。

[⬆ back to top](#)

## 移除软件包

```shell
sudo apt remove <package>
```

该命令用于移除指定的软件包。它会将软件包及其相关的配置文件从系统中删除。

[⬆ back to top](#)

## 搜索软件包

```shell
apt search <keyword>
```

该命令用于搜索包含指定关键字的软件包。它会列出与关键字相关的软件包名称和描述。

[⬆ back to top](#)

## 显示软件包信息

```shell
apt show <package>
```

该命令用于显示指定软件包的详细信息，包括版本号、依赖关系、描述等。

[⬆ back to top](#)

## 更新软件包源列表

```shell
sudp apt update
```

它是在使用APT进行软件包管理时非常重要的一步。当你运行apt update命令时，APT会连接到配置的软件包源服务器，并下载最新的软件包列表信息。这些软件包列表包含了可用的软件包和它们的版本信息。

下面是 `apt update` 命令的作用：

-   **更新软件包列表**：apt update命令会更新本地系统中的软件包列表。软件包列表是一个包含可用软件包的索引，它包含了软件包的名称、版本、依赖关系等重要信息。通过更新软件包列表，你可以了解到最新的软件包和版本信息。

-   **获取最新的软件包版本**：通过运行apt update命令，你可以获取最新的软件包版本信息。APT会检查软件包源服务器上的软件包，并比较本地系统中已安装的软件包版本与软件包源上的最新版本。这有助于确定是否有可用的更新版本供你安装。

-   **解决软件包依赖关系**：软件包之间存在依赖关系，即某些软件包需要依赖其他软件包才能正常工作。通过运行apt update命令，APT会检查软件包源上的依赖关系并更新本地系统的软件包列表。这有助于确保软件包的依赖关系得到满足，以便正确地安装和更新软件包。

使用`apt`命令时，不需要在命令后面添加`sudo apt-get`中常见的`sudo`和`get`关键字。它提供了更简洁的语法，并且在处理依赖关系时更加智能和自动化。这使得软件包的安装和管理过程更加便捷和高效。

## 其他

```shell

searching and managing as well as querying information about packages.
It provides the same functionality as the specialized APT tools,
like apt-get and apt-cache, but enables options more suitable for
interactive use by default.

Most used commands:
  list - list packages based on package names
  search - search in package descriptions
  show - show package details
  install - install packages

```

[⬆ back to top](#)

# 配置

在上面有提到使用 `apt install <package>` 安装软件，对此不禁有疑问：所安装的软件的来源是那里获取的？

实际上，APT（Advanced Packaging Tool）通过软件源（Software Repository）来获取和安装软件包。软件源是一个集中存储软件包的远程服务器，APT通过访问这些服务器来搜索、下载和安装软件包。

在系统中配置了软件源列表（source list）后，APT 会根据列表中的地址和设置来确定可用的软件源服务器。

[⬆ back to top](#)

## 软件源

软件源是存储软件包和更新的服务器或存储库。它是用户获取并安装软件的主要来源之一。软件源提供了一个集中的位置，用户可以从中获取各种软件包、应用程序和系统组件，以满足其Linux操作系统的需求。

以下是一些常见的软件源类型，它们广泛用于不同的Linux发行版：

-   官方软件源；

-   第三方软件源；

-   Snap Store；

-   Flatpak。

[⬆ back to top](#)

### 官方软件源

各Linux发行版都维护了自己的官方软件源，提供了核心软件包和更新。例如：

-   Ubuntu：https://packages.ubuntu.com/

-   Debian：https://packages.debian.org/

-   Fedora：https://apps.fedoraproject.org/packages/

-   CentOS：https://www.centos.org/packages/

-   Arch Linux：https://archlinux.org/packages/

-   openSUSE：https://software.opensuse.org/

-   Mageia：https://madb.mageia.org/

-   Gentoo：https://packages.gentoo.org/

这些链接将带你到相应发行版的官方软件源的网页，你可以使用这些网页来搜索和浏览软件包列表。请注意，这些链接可能会随着时间变化而更新，所以最好通过搜索引擎或官方网站来获取最新的软件源链接。

[⬆ back to top](#)

### 第三方软件源

许多开发者、社区和组织维护自己的软件源，提供特定软件的最新版本和增强功能。这些第三方软件源可以是针对特定软件的官方源，也可以是由社区维护的源。常见的第三方软件源如：

-   [Ubuntu PPA（Personal Package Archive）](https://launchpad.net/ubuntu/+ppas)：个人软件仓库，由Ubuntu用户创建和维护。提供了额外的软件包和更新。

-   [RPM Fusion（适用于Fedora和CentOS）](https://rpmfusion.org/)：提供了一些常用软件的补充包，包括多媒体相关的软件和驱动程序。

-   [Arch User Repository（AUR）](https://aur.archlinux.org/)（适用于Arch Linux）：由Arch Linux社区维护的软件仓库，允许用户共享和安装自定义软件包。

-   [OBS（Open Build Service）](https://build.opensuse.org/)（适用于多个发行版）：一个开放的软件构建服务，允许开发者构建和发布软件包。支持多个Linux发行版。

-   [EPEL（Extra Packages for Enterprise Linux）](https://fedoraproject.org/wiki/EPEL)（适用于CentOS和RHEL）：为企业级Linux发行版提供额外的软件包，以满足更广泛的需求。

-   [Nixpkgs（适用于NixOS）](https://nixos.org/nixpkgs/)：NixOS的官方软件仓库，提供了丰富的软件包和配置管理工具。

-   [Homebrew](https://brew.sh/)（适用于macOS）：macOS上的包管理器，提供了易于安装和管理的软件包。

这些第三方软件源提供了额外的软件包和功能，使用户能够获取更多的选择和定制性。请注意，使用第三方软件源时应谨慎，确保了解源的可信度和安全性，并遵循它们的使用指南。

[⬆ back to top](#)

### Snap Store

[Snap Store](https://snapcraft.io/store) 是一个官方的软件分发平台，它提供了广泛的应用程序和工具，适用于基于 Linux 的各种发行版，如 Ubuntu、Fedora、CentOS、Arch Linux等。Snap Store基于Snap包管理系统，这是一种跨发行版的软件打包和分发格式。

Snap Store的特点包括：

1.  跨发行版支持：Snap Store的软件包可以在多种不同的Linux发行版上安装和运行，无需担心依赖关系或兼容性问题。

2.  安全性：Snap包采用沙箱技术，提供了额外的安全层，确保软件的隔离性和安全性。每个Snap应用程序都有自己的依赖和运行环境，不会干扰系统的其他部分。

3.  自动更新：Snap Store中的软件包会自动更新到最新版本，确保用户始终使用最新的功能和修复的bug。

4.  宽广的应用程序库：Snap Store提供了各种类型的应用程序，包括办公套件、多媒体工具、开发工具、游戏等，使用户能够方便地找到并安装他们所需的软件。

在Snap Store中，你可以浏览不同类别的软件，搜索特定的应用程序，并通过简单的几个步骤安装和管理它们。

[⬆ back to top](#)

#### 使用

```shell
# 安装 snapd
sudo apt update
sudo apt install snapd
sudo snap install core

# 安装软件
sudo snap install <package>

# 删除软件
sudo snap remove <package>

# 查看已安装软件
sudo snap list
```

### Flatpak

[Flatpak](https://flathub.org/) 是一个用于Linux发行版的软件打包和分发系统，类似于Snap。它提供了一种跨发行版的方式，允许开发者打包应用程序及其依赖项，并在不同的Linux发行版上以沙箱环境中运行。

Flatpak的特点包括：

1.  跨发行版支持：Flatpak允许开发者将应用程序打包为独立的容器，与底层系统无关。这使得应用程序可以在各种不同的Linux发行版上运行，无需重新打包。

2.  沙箱环境：Flatpak应用程序运行在沙箱环境中，与系统其他部分隔离。这提供了额外的安全性，防止应用程序对系统造成潜在的影响。

3.  应用程序库：Flatpak通过Flathub提供了一个中央应用程序库，其中包含了大量的应用程序供用户选择。你可以在Flathub上浏览各种类别的应用程序，并通过几个简单的步骤安装它们。

4.  更新管理：Flatpak应用程序可以自动更新，确保用户始终使用最新的版本和修复的漏洞。

使用Flatpak，你可以浏览Flathub上的应用程序，搜索特定的应用程序，并使用Flatpak命令行工具或图形界面工具进行安装、更新和管理。Flatpak提供了一种简便的方式，使用户能够轻松地获取和运行各种Linux应用程序。

[⬆ back to top](#)

#### 使用

```shell
# 安装 flatpak 完成后，重启生效
sudo apt install flatpak
flatpak remote-add --if-not-exists flathub https://dl.flathub.org/repo/flathub.flatpakrepo

# 安装软件
flatpak install flathub <package>
```

## 配置文件

这些软件源的地址被配置在 `/etc/apt/sources.list` 或 `/etc/apt/sources.list.d/`目录下的`*.list`文件中。

-   `source.list` 文件定义了一个或多个软件源的URL，软件包管理器将从这些源中下载软件包。每个源的URL通常指向一个包含软件包的软件存储库。

-   `source.list.d/` 目录是 `/etc/apt/` 目录下的另一个目录，用于存放以 `.list` 为扩展名的软件源文件。这个目录允许用户和软件包管理器将软件源的配置拆分为多个文件，以便更好地组织和管理。可以通过简单地在该目录中创建一个新的.list文件来添加新的软件源。这种分割的方式使得在不影响source.list文件的情况下添加、删除或修改软件源变得更加方便，而无需修改单个大文件。

例如：

```shell
├── sources.list
└── sources.list.d
    ├── cloudflare-client.list
    ├── microsoft-edge.list
    └── vscode.list
```

[⬆ back to top](#)

## 优先级

在 Debian 和 Ubuntu 等 Linux 发行版中，`source.list`文件和`source.list.d/`目录下的`.list`文件中的配置具有以下优先级：

1.  `source.list.d/`目录下的`.list`文件的优先级高于`source.list`文件。这意味着如果在`source.list.d/`目录中存在与`source.list`中相同的软件源配置，将使用`source.list.d/`目录中的配置。

2.  当存在多个`source.list.d/`目录下的`.list`文件时，它们的加载顺序是按照文件名的字母顺序进行的。较早加载的文件中的配置将被后续加载的文件中的配置覆盖。

3.  如果存在相同软件源的重复配置，后面加载的配置将覆盖先前加载的配置。因此，在`source.list.d/`目录中的较晚加载的`.list`文件中的配置将覆盖较早加载的文件中相同软件源的配置。

需要注意的是，优先级仅适用于软件源配置。对于其他APT设置（如代理配置、密钥管理等），在`source.list`中配置的设置将始终具有最高优先级。

[⬆ back to top](#)

## 配置格式

下面是 Debian 12 的 `source.list` 配置内容：

```shell
# isaac @ debian in /etc/apt [13:26:09] C:130
$ cat sources.list

deb https://mirrors.tuna.tsinghua.edu.cn/debian/ bookworm main contrib non-free non-free-firmware
deb-src https://mirrors.tuna.tsinghua.edu.cn/debian/ bookworm main contrib non-free non-free-firmware

deb https://mirrors.tuna.tsinghua.edu.cn/debian/ bookworm-updates main contrib non-free non-free-firmware
deb-src https://mirrors.tuna.tsinghua.edu.cn/debian/ bookworm-updates main contrib non-free non-free-firmware

deb https://mirrors.tuna.tsinghua.edu.cn/debian/ bookworm-backports main contrib non-free non-free-firmware
deb-src https://mirrors.tuna.tsinghua.edu.cn/debian/ bookworm-backports main contrib non-free non-free-firmware

# deb https://mirrors.tuna.tsinghua.edu.cn/debian-security bookworm-security main contrib non-free non-free-firmware
# deb-src https://mirrors.tuna.tsinghua.edu.cn/debian-security bookworm-security main contrib non-free non-free-firmware

deb https://security.debian.org/debian-security bookworm-security main contrib non-free non-free-firmware
deb-src https://security.debian.org/debian-security bookworm-security main contrib non-free non-free-firmware
```

以上面的 `sources.list` 文件的第一行为例说明一个软件源的配置格式：

```shell
deb https://mirrors.tuna.tsinghua.edu.cn/debian/ bookworm main contrib non-free non-free-firmware

<软件源关键词> <软件源地址> <发行版名称> <组件1> <组件2> ...
```

它指定了一个名为"bookworm"的发行版，使用了清华大学开源软件镜像站（https://mirrors.tuna.tsinghua.edu.cn/debian/）作为软件源。

[⬆ back to top](#)

### 软件源关键词

`deb`：这是APT软件源配置中的关键词，表示这是一个二进制包的软件源。

软件源配置中常用的关键词有以下几个：

1.  **deb**：表示这是一个二进制包的软件源。

2.  **deb-src**：表示这是一个源代码包的软件源。

这两个关键词用于不同类型的软件源，前者用于获取和安装二进制包，后者用于获取和构建源代码包。

[⬆ back to top](#)

### 软件源地址

`https://mirrors.tuna.tsinghua.edu.cn/debian/`：这是软件源的URL地址，指向清华大学开源软件镜像站的 Debian 软件源。

这里的清华源并非默认的源，默认的官方源是 `http://deb.debian.org/debian/`，由于访问官网源在国内比较慢等原因，因此上面使用了国内的源。除了清华源外，国内还有其他 Debian APT 源，常见的有：

-   [腾讯软件源](https://mirrors.cloud.tencent.com/)

-   [阿里源](https://developer.aliyun.com/mirror/)

-   [华为源](https://mirrors.huaweicloud.com/home)

-   [中科大源](http://mirrors.ustc.edu.cn/)

[⬆ back to top](#)

### 发行版名称

`bookworm`：这是发行版的名称，表示这个软件源适用于 Debian 12（代码名称为"Bookworm"）。

更多的 Debian 的发行版本名称见 [附录](#Debian-的发行版本名称)

[⬆ back to top](#)

### 组件

`main contrib non-free non-free-firmware`： 这是软件源中的组件。不同的组件包含了不同类型的软件包。

-   **main**：Debian 发行版的核心组件，包含了自由的开源软件包。

-   **contrib**：这是非必需的软件包组件，包含了依赖于main组件的一些软件包。

-   **non-free**：这是非自由软件包组件，包含了不符合自由软件定义的软件包。

-   **non-free-firmware**：这是非自由的硬件固件组件，包含了一些设备所需的非自由固件。

[⬆ back to top](#)

## 小结

软件源列表（Source List）是一个文本文件，用于配置系统中软件包管理器（如APT）的软件源服务器信息。它包含了系统用于下载和安装软件包的网络地址。

在 Debian 系及其衍生发行版（如Ubuntu）中，软件源列表文件通常位于`/etc/apt/sources.list`或`/etc/apt/sources.list.d/`目录下。这个文件中列出了各种软件源服务器的地址，以及与每个软件源相关的软件包分发渠道和组件。

软件源列表文件的内容可以根据用户的需求进行自定义。用户可以根据自己的地理位置、网络速度和软件需求来选择合适的软件源服务器。通过编辑软件源列表文件，用户可以添加、删除或更改软件源，以便获取所需的软件包。

在使用APT进行软件包管理时，软件源列表起到关键作用。通过配置正确的软件源，系统可以正确地下载和安装软件包，保持系统的更新和安全。因此，了解软件源列表的概念并正确配置它是非常重要的。

[⬆ back to top](#)

# 总结

这是一篇关于 Linux 系统中 APT 包管理器的使用指南。本文主要内容如下:

第一部分介绍了 APT 的基本概念，它是 Debian 系统及其衍生发行版中的常用包管理工具，通过 apt 命令提供软件包管理功能。

第二部分详细解释了 APT 的各种常用命令，包括安装、升级、删除、搜索、显示软件包信息等，并给出了具体的命令格式和使用示例，便于读者快速掌握。

第三部分着重讲解了 APT 的软件源配置，包括不同类型软件源、它们之间的优先级关系、sources.list 文件的格式等内容。正确配置软件源对 APT 的正常使用非常关键。

[⬆ back to top](#)
